title: A Conversation About Forgiving a Friend Who Spread a Rumor
script: Dina: [hesitant] Wulan, can we talk? I heard that you told everyone at the office I was the reason the project got delayed, even though that wasn't true at all.
Wulan: [ashamed] I know, Dina, and I have been dreading this conversation since I found out you heard about it.
Dina: [hurt] Why would you say something like that, especially when you knew the delay was actually caused by the client changing their requirements twice?
Wulan: [regretful] Honestly, I was frustrated that our manager blamed the whole team, and instead of explaining calmly, I panicked and pointed at you without thinking it through.
Dina: [tense] Do you realize how that made me look in front of people I have worked with for three years?
Wulan: [sincerely] I do, and there is no excuse that makes it acceptable, even though I wish I could explain away what I did.
Dina: [reflective] Part of me wants to stay angry, because trust like this takes years to build and only a moment to damage.
Wulan: [pleading] I understand if you need time. I have already told our manager the truth today, even though it was uncomfortable to admit I was wrong.
Dina: [surprised] You corrected it already? I did not expect you to take responsibility that quickly.
Wulan: [honestly] If I had stayed silent, the misunderstanding would only have grown larger, and you would have kept carrying blame that was never yours to begin with.
Dina: [softening] That does matter to me, more than an apology alone would have. Actions like that are harder to fake than words.
Wulan: [hopeful] I am not asking you to forget what happened, but I hope that, given time, we can rebuild the trust I damaged.
Dina: [thoughtful] Forgiveness does not mean pretending nothing happened, Wulan. It means choosing not to let this one mistake define how I see you.
Wulan: [relieved] Thank you for even considering that. I promise the next time I feel frustrated, I will speak to you directly instead of talking around you.
Dina: [warmly] Good. Despite everything, I would rather keep working alongside someone who admits their mistakes than someone who never makes them at all.
Wulan: [grateful] I will try to earn that trust back, one honest moment at a time.

quiz.question: What did Wulan tell people at the office?
options: That Dina was the reason the project got delayed
That Dina made a mistake in a report
quiz.explanation: Wulan told everyone at the office that Dina was the reason the project got delayed, which wasn't true.

quiz.question: What actually caused the project delay?
options: The client changing their requirements twice
quiz.explanation: Dina points out the delay was actually caused by the client changing their requirements twice.

quiz.question: Why did Wulan blame Dina in the first place?
options: She genuinely believed it was Dina's fault
She panicked when the manager blamed the whole team and pointed at Dina without thinking
Someone told her to say it
quiz.explanation: Wulan admits she panicked when frustrated about the manager blaming the whole team, and pointed at Dina without thinking it through.

quiz.question: What had Wulan already done before this conversation?
options: Asked someone else to apologize for her
quiz.explanation: Wulan had already told their manager the truth that day, even though it was uncomfortable to admit.

quiz.question: How does Dina define forgiveness at the end?
options: Choosing not to let one mistake define how she sees Wulan
quiz.explanation: Dina says forgiveness means choosing not to let this one mistake define how she sees Wulan, not pretending nothing happened.
